source.title: 象棋局面读数样例（文件自述：模拟样例，供测试判定用，非真实抓取）

parameters.row_origin: row 0 is the black home rank

required_evidence: a real screen capture of a xiangqi board rather than the bundled simulated sample
rules.engineering_scope: The state.board array is read as 10 rows of 9 cells with row 0 on the black home rank. Only geometry is granted; nothing here authorises a move or a legal-position judgement.

source_entries: 棋子前缀 b=黑方 r=红方

parameters.token_form: single-letter side prefix followed by one piece glyph

required_evidence: a real capture whose side prefix is confirmed against the rendered colour of the piece
rules.engineering_scope: The leading character of every non-empty cell assigns the piece to a side. The exporter's side map consumes this; no gameplay consequence is asserted.

required_evidence: a real capture where an empty intersection is confirmed empty rather than merely unread
rules.engineering_scope: A null cell is an empty intersection and yields no annotation unit. An unread cell must not be collapsed into this representation; that distinction stays unvalidated.

required_evidence: a rules source stating whether the paired glyphs share movement law
a capture of the opposite-colour setup
rules.engineering_scope: Both armies use different glyphs for the general, the adviser and the elephant; the other four names are shared. Observed in the sample array. Whether the glyph pairs are movement-equivalent is not evidenced here and is not assumed.

source_entries: 模拟样例，供测试判定用，非真实抓取
required_evidence: an authoritative competition-rules text for the initial array
a real capture taken before the first move
rules.engineering_scope: The sample array is measured and is internally symmetric, which is what an opening setup looks like. The file itself declares the board a simulated sample, so this registers an observation, not a confirmed opening rule, and no engine consumes it.

required_evidence: a real capture where the recorded move is replayed against the preceding board
a source defining whose turn follows a recorded move
rules.engineering_scope: A recorded move is expected to show up in the board array and to flip the side to move. The bundled sample contradicts both: the red cannons are still on their original files and turn still reads red. Recorded as an open gap, not as accepted behaviour.

required_evidence: a capture corpus containing both values
a rules source for whose turn it is after each side moves
rules.engineering_scope: One side-token slot is read and annotated. Its value domain and its relation to move legality are not established by anything in this repository.

parameters.observed_shape: piece glyph + file + direction verb + file

required_evidence: an authoritative notation source covering the full verb and file set
several recorded moves of both armies
rules.engineering_scope: The last-move slot carries a Chinese-notation string. One sample string evidences the shape, not the grammar, so nothing parses it into a source and destination.

required_evidence: a rules source defining the check condition
a capture of a position that is actually in check
rules.engineering_scope: A boolean check slot is read and labelled. The sample only ever shows false, so the condition that would set it true is unverified and no check detection is claimed.

required_evidence: a capture taken immediately after a piece is lost
a source fixing what recent means here
rules.engineering_scope: The slot exists and is nullable; a null yields no annotation unit. Because it is never populated in the evidence, neither its shape nor its window is verified.

required_evidence: a primary rules source for each piece's movement law, held in this repository and pinned by digest
a per-piece legal-move generator to bind engine_status to
rules.engineering_scope: Reserved for the per-piece movement laws of the game. No in-repo artifact states them, so this rule carries no anchor and grants nothing: it is a declared hole, kept visible instead of being filled with a borrowed or invented citation.

required_evidence: a primary rules source covering checkmate, stalemate and repetition
device evidence of an ending being reached
rules.engineering_scope: Reserved for how a game ends. The evidence surface exposes only an in-check boolean, which is not enough to derive an outcome, so no ending rule is claimed.
